title: Microsoft Purview: Microsoft Graph APIs for archive mailboxes as EWS retires
summary: The migration deadline, rollout dates, archive redirect behaviour, licensing and both control rows are supported. One minor qualification remains: Microsoft's two EWS control pages disagree about per-user exceptions to organisation-wide blocking.

claims.claim: Microsoft is adding Graph access to main archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: Access to Archive mailboxes (Main + Auxiliary) through Microsoft Graph.

claims.claim: The planned Graph archive access includes auxiliary archives.
claims.quote: Access to Archive mailboxes (Main + Auxiliary) through Microsoft Graph.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a single seamless archive view across auxiliary mailboxes.
claims.quote: The goal is to give users a single, seamless Archive view, even though Archive data may physically reside across multiple auxiliary mailboxes

claims.claim: MC1469565 says Graph now supports importing and exporting mailbox data.
claims.quote: Microsoft Graph now provides API support for importing and exporting mailbox data

claims.claim: MC1469565 says Graph supports archive folder management, including auto-expanding archives.
claims.quote: and for managing archive mailbox folders, including support for auto-expanding archives.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving creates auxiliary archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: An archive mailbox can include a main archive mailbox and one or more auxiliary archive mailboxes (created through autoexpanding archive).

claims.claim: A folder can appear in the main archive while its contents reside in an auxiliary archive.
claims.quote: In some cases, a folder appears in the main archive mailbox, but its contents actually reside in an auxiliary archive mailbox.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Accessing an auxiliary archive folder can return HTTP 308 Permanent Redirect.
claims.quote: When you access a folder that physically resides in an auxiliary archive mailbox, the API returns an HTTP 308 Permanent Redirect with a Location header.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Exporting auto-expanded archive items can return ErrorArchiveFolderMovedPermanently for individual items.
claims.quote: When you export items from a mailbox that has autoexpanded archive folders, some items in the response might include an ErrorArchiveFolderMovedPermanently error instead of data.

claims.claim: The application retries redirected folder and export requests using the URL supplied in the response.
claims.quote: Your app makes a new request to the URL indicated in the response.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: An import into a folder physically located in an auxiliary archive returns HTTP 409 Conflict identifying the target mailbox.
claims.quote: When you attempt to import an item into a folder that physically resides in an auxiliary (autoexpanded) archive mailbox, you receive an HTTP 409 Conflict response that indicates the correct target mailbox.

claims.claim: Resolving the import conflict requires a new import session targeting the mailbox named in the error.
claims.quote: To resolve this issue, create a new import session targeting the mailbox ID indicated in the error message

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Well-known folder names are not supported for archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: Well-known folder names aren't supported for archive mailboxes.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Applications must reference archive folders by folder ID.
claims.quote: Reference folders in archive mailboxes by folder ID rather than by well-known folder name.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Applications and scripts retaining EWS archive operations stop working after EWS is disabled.
claims.quote: Applications and scripts that continue to use EWS for archive mailbox operations will stop functioning after EWS is disabled.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Affected examples include eDiscovery, compliance, records management, data lifecycle management, backup, export and custom archive applications.
claims.quote: eDiscovery solutions- Compliance and records management workflows- Data lifecycle management solutions- Backup and export tools- Custom applications that access archive mailboxes

claims.claim: The Message Center compliance table confirms possible interruption of Purview-related workflows.
claims.quote: Yes. Organizations using EWS-based integrations for eDiscovery, compliance exports, retention-related processes, or data lifecycle management that access archive mailboxes must migrate to Microsoft Graph APIs before EWS is disabled.

claims.claim: The default state of Graph archive API enablement is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Graph" "archive mailboxes" "default"; "archive" "Graph" "tenant" "enable" mailbox import export default. Read roadmap, MC1469565, archive redirects and both mailbox import/export overviews; none states a default or an administrator enablement requirement.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant-level switch specifically enabling or disabling the Graph archive APIs is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "archive" "Graph" "tenant-level" switch; "archive" "Graph" "tenant" "enable" mailbox import export default. Opened archive redirects, both import/export overviews, exportItems and List folders; no API-specific tenant switch was documented.

claims.claim: No further consequence of inaction beyond EWS disablement and its effects is stated.
claims.quote: Searched: EWS archive vendor fees; EWS usage report Microsoft Graph API PowerShell Exchange weekly usage report programmatic. Read MC1469565 and Learn's EWS deprecation page: they describe disablement, failing integrations and migration, without a separate additional consequence.

claims.claim: Graph mailbox export preserves items in full fidelity.
claims.quote: These items can be exported as an opaque stream in full fidelity (you can't change the export stream).

claims.claim: Exported items can be imported into the same or a different mailbox.
claims.quote: Items can be imported to the same mailbox or a different one.

claims.claim: The mailbox import/export APIs are not designed for mailbox backup and restore.
claims.quote: The mailbox import and export APIs in Microsoft Graph aren't designed for mailbox backup and restore.

claims.claim: User-agent-based EWS blocking also affects REST and Graph connections.
claims.quote: Note: User Agent based blocking also impacts connections using REST/Graph API

claims.claim: The tenant EWS usage report is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Usage > Reports > Exchange > EWS usage.
claims.quote:
In the navigation menu, select Reports. If you don't see Reports, select Show all, and then select Reports.
Select Usage.
On the Usage page, under Reports, select Exchange.
On the report page, select the EWS usage tab.

claims.claim: No programmatic equivalent of the EWS usage report is documented, and the Graph usage reports list contains no EWS report.
